analysis: Reviewed base-text excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 3778-5074) plus the patch excerpt. The visible changes are mechanical regenerations of public synthetic golden vectors: prompt_contract_id changes from 6bb9fb05... to 8171fec3... in the model entry and per-case plan blocks, along with chain_hash values for block_boundaries. Within the supplied excerpts, only the base side is shown for the changed lines (e.g. 3944, 3949, 3953, 3957, 3960, 4862-4882); the head side and the full range map (range_map_complete=false) are not visible. Inputs are public synthetic text ('Public synthetic cache-parity input', 'cache cache...') with no secrets, real prompts, credentials or keys. The fixture is test data and has no runtime authorization, attestation or encryption effect. The relevant threat is T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing): the prompt_contract_id and chain_hash values feed prefix-cache keying, so a consistent contract-ID change is a correctness and cache-isolation concern, not a vulnerability in the JSON itself. Unverified contracts: (1) that the new prompt_contract_id and chain hashes match what the Swift provider and any coordinator implementation compute; (2) that the provider code which defines the prompt contract was changed in this PR in lockstep; (3) that any contract-version bump invalidates old encrypted SSD cache artifacts so stale prefix caches cannot be reused across template changes. These sit in files outside this batch. No concrete security regression is identified from the supplied evidence, and no threat-model assumption is invalidated. Deeper review is only needed if the provider-side prompt contract and cache-key code changed in other batches.
